## Summary
Pressing Enter to submit a new sub-task triggers a duplicate creation because the Enter keydown handler and the container's focusout handler both call \`submitSubtask()\` — the focusout fires when the input row is unmounted after the first submit. Fix also addresses two accessibility gaps found during UX review.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1: Enter creates exactly one sub-task
- **Given** the sub-task creation row is open with a non-empty title
- **When** the user presses Enter
- **Then** exactly one sub-task is created with the typed title

### AC2: Focusout still submits when Enter was not used
- **Given** the sub-task creation row is open with a non-empty title
- **When** the user clicks or tabs focus outside the creation row (without pressing Enter)
- **Then** exactly one sub-task is created with the typed title

### AC3: Escape cancels without creating any sub-task
- **Given** the sub-task creation row is open with a non-empty title
- **When** the user presses Escape
- **Then** no sub-task is created and the creation row closes

### AC4: Multiple sub-tasks can be added in sequence
- **Given** the user has already submitted one sub-task via Enter
- **When** the user clicks "+ Add" again, types a new title, and presses Enter
- **Then** the second sub-task is created exactly once (the guard resets between sessions)

### AC5: Empty or whitespace input creates no sub-task on Enter or focusout
- **Given** the sub-task creation row is open with an empty or whitespace-only title
- **When** the user presses Enter or focus leaves the row
- **Then** no sub-task is created and the creation row closes

### AC6: Sub-task title input has an accessible name (UX — accepted)
- **Given** the sub-task creation row is open
- **When** a screen reader focuses the title input
- **Then** the input has an accessible name (aria-label="Sub-task title") independent of placeholder text

### AC7: Sub-task creation row meets touch target height on mobile (UX — accepted)
- **Given** the app is viewed on a mobile viewport (≤768px)
- **When** the sub-task creation row is visible
- **Then** the row has a minimum height of 44px

## Scope

### In Scope
- Fixing the double-submit bug in `card-detail.tsx`
- Adding `aria-label="Sub-task title"` to the title input (AC6)
- Adding `min-height: 44px` to `.subtask-add-inline` in the mobile breakpoint in `global.css` (AC7)
- Regression tests for all ACs

### Out of Scope
- Adding explicit Add/Cancel buttons to the creation row (deferred)
- Sub-task title truncation on mobile (deferred)
- Keyboard hint text (deferred)
- Changes to the Apps Script backend or business rules

## Technical Notes
- **Files likely affected:** `frontend/src/components/board/card-detail.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/board/card-detail.test.tsx`, `frontend/src/global.css`
- **Complexity:** small (2 source files + 1 CSS, targeted changes)
- **Rules sync required:** no
- **Root cause:** `handleCreationRowFocusOut` calls `submitSubtask()` after Enter already called it, because the input unmounting fires `focusout` before Preact's batched state update clears `subtaskTitle`. Fix: a `useRef` boolean guard set in `submitSubtask` (and `cancelSubtask`) and checked at the top of `handleCreationRowFocusOut`, reset in `handleAddSubtask`.

## Open Questions
- None

## Summary
Add an optional scheduled date picker to the create-item modal so users can set when they plan to work on a task at creation time, without needing to edit it afterward.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1: Scheduled date picker present in create modal
- **Given** the user opens the "New Item" modal
- **When** the modal renders
- **Then** there is an optional "Scheduled Date" date input field between "Due Date" and "Labels", with hint text "When you plan to do this" beneath the label

### AC2: Creating an item with a scheduled date
- **Given** the user has opened the create modal and filled in a title
- **When** they select a scheduled date and click "Create"
- **Then** the item is created with the scheduled_date persisted to the Items sheet

### AC3: Creating an item without a scheduled date
- **Given** the user has opened the create modal and filled in a title
- **When** they leave the scheduled date empty and click "Create"
- **Then** the item is created with an empty scheduled_date (no error, no default value)

### AC4: Scheduled date round-trips to card detail
- **Given** the user created an item with a scheduled date
- **When** they open the card detail panel for that item
- **Then** the scheduled date field shows the date they set during creation

### AC5: Accessible labeling
- **Given** a screen reader user navigates the create modal
- **When** they reach the scheduled date input
- **Then** the input has a programmatically associated label via matching id/for attributes

## Scope

### In Scope
- Add `scheduledDate` state and `<input type="date">` to the create-item modal
- Pass `scheduled_date` through to the `createItem` action
- Hint text beneath the label for clarity vs Due Date
- Proper label/input association for accessibility

### Out of Scope
- Date validation (no past-date blocking, no scheduled-before-due enforcement)
- Quick-select shortcuts (today, tomorrow, next week)
- Date+time support (date only, matching existing Due Date pattern)
- Collapsible/advanced sections in the form
- Changes to how scheduled_date displays on cards or in the detail panel
- Changes to business rules or rules sync

## Technical Notes
- **Files likely affected:** `frontend/src/components/forms/create-item-modal.tsx` (add state + input field + pass to createItem)
- **Complexity:** small — single file change, follows existing Due Date pattern exactly
- **Rules sync required:** no — no new business rules
- **Dependencies:** none — the data model, API layer, backend, and detail panel already support scheduled_date fully

## Open Questions
None — all original questions resolved:
- **Date vs date+time?** Date only (matches existing Due Date pattern)
- **Quick-select options?** Out of scope for this issue
- **Layout room?** UX review confirms 6 fields fit without scrolling on mobile (520px total vs 600px+ available)

## Summary
Allow logged-in users to edit their display name via a profile dialog accessible from the header. The new name is persisted in the existing Owners sheet and reflected everywhere on the board.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1: Profile trigger in header
- **Given** a logged-in user viewing the board
- **When** the board loads
- **Then** the user's Google avatar and display name appear in the header as a `<button>` element with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, a visible hover/focus state, and a minimum 44x44px touch target on mobile viewports
- **And** if the display name exceeds the available header space, it truncates with an ellipsis

### AC2: Open profile dialog
- **Given** a logged-in user
- **When** they click (or activate via Enter/Space) the profile trigger in the header
- **Then** a modal dialog opens with `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and a descriptive `aria-label`
- **And** the dialog shows: the user's Google profile picture (decorative, `alt=""`), their Google email (read-only with label), and an editable display name input (pre-filled with current name, with associated `<label>`)
- **And** focus moves to the display name input and a focus trap is active (Tab/Shift+Tab cycle within the dialog)

### AC3: Save display name
- **Given** the profile dialog is open with a valid new display name
- **When** the user clicks "Save"
- **Then** the Save button shows a loading state and is disabled to prevent double-submission
- **And** Cancel, Escape, and overlay click are suppressed while the save is in flight
- **And** the Owners sheet `name` column is updated for the user's email via `upsertOwner`
- **And** all Items with the old owner name have their `owner` field updated to the new name (cascade update)
- **And** the in-memory owners signal and items signal refresh to reflect the change
- **And** the dialog closes, focus returns to the profile trigger, and a toast confirms "Display name updated"
- **And** if the save fails, the dialog remains open with an inline error message and the Save button re-enables so the user can retry

### AC4: Display name validation
- **Given** the profile dialog is open
- **When** the user attempts to save an empty, whitespace-only, or >50 character display name
- **Then** an inline validation error appears below the input, associated via `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid="true"`
- **And** the Save button remains enabled but the save is prevented until the error is resolved
- **And** newlines and control characters are stripped from the input on save

### AC5: Cancel / dismiss without saving
- **Given** the profile dialog is open (with or without unsaved changes) and no save is in flight
- **When** the user clicks "Cancel", presses Escape, or clicks the overlay backdrop
- **Then** the dialog closes without persisting changes and focus returns to the profile trigger
- **And** no unsaved-changes confirmation is shown (intentional simplicity for a low-frequency action)

### AC6: Keyboard and screen reader accessibility
- **Given** a keyboard-only or screen reader user
- **When** they interact with the profile feature
- **Then** the profile trigger is focusable and activatable via Enter/Space
- **And** the dialog uses the existing `useFocusTrap` hook pattern (matching `CardDetail`)
- **And** the close button has `aria-label="Close"`
- **And** validation errors are announced to screen readers

## Scope

### In Scope
- Profile dialog UI (modal pattern matching `CreateItemModal` / `CardDetail`)
- Editable display name field with validation (empty, whitespace, >50 chars, control characters)
- Persist name change to Owners sheet via existing `upsertOwner` API
- Cascade owner name update across all matching Items in the sheet
- Update header trigger from passive `<div>` to accessible `<button>`
- Loading state on Save, toast on success, inline error on failure
- Dismiss suppression while save is in flight
- Focus management (trap, return) and ARIA attributes
- Long name truncation with ellipsis in the header
- Demo mode support (mock profile dialog behavior)

### Out of Scope
- Additional profile fields (avatar upload, color theme, preferences)
- Duplicate name warning/prevention (allowed -- family members may share names)
- "Reset to Google name" button (future enhancement)
- Apps Script backend changes (frontend-only feature -- direct Sheets API)
- Profile picture editing

## UX Consultation

### Critical (must address -- incorporated into ACs above)
1. **Profile trigger must be a `<button>`, not a `<div>`** -- the current `.user-info` div in `kanban-board.tsx` (lines 93-99) has no `tabindex`, `role`, or key handler. A `<button>` gives keyboard focusability, Enter/Space activation, and correct screen reader semantics for free. Add `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and visible hover/focus states. *(AC1, AC6)*
2. **Dialog ARIA attributes** -- must have `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and `aria-label="User Profile"` (following the `CardDetail` pattern at lines 142-147). *(AC2)*
3. **Focus trap and return** -- use the existing `useFocusTrap` hook. On open, focus the display name input. On close, return focus to the profile trigger button. *(AC2, AC3, AC5, AC6)*
4. **Validation error association** -- inline errors must use `aria-describedby` pointing to the error element and `aria-invalid="true"` on the input. Existing `--color-danger: #d32f2f` passes contrast (5.6:1 against white). *(AC4)*

### Recommended (should address -- incorporated into ACs above)
5. **Loading/disabled state on Save** -- prevent double-submission during the `upsertOwner` + cascade API calls. Suppress Cancel/Escape while save is in flight. *(AC3)*
6. **Overlay click to close** -- both `CreateItemModal` (line 44) and `CardDetail` (line 148) close on overlay click. Profile dialog should match. *(AC5)*
7. **50-character max length** -- prevents abuse and Google Sheets cell overflow. Show inline error if exceeded. *(AC4)*
8. **Mobile touch target** -- profile trigger must be at least 44x44px on viewports below 768px (WCAG 2.5.5). *(AC1)*
9. **Header name truncation** -- long display names should truncate with ellipsis to prevent header overflow. *(AC1)*
10. **Error recovery** -- if save fails, keep dialog open with inline error and re-enable Save for retry. *(AC3)*
11. **Strip control characters** -- newlines and control characters stripped from input on save. *(AC4)*

### Enhancement (nice to have, out of scope for now)
12. Character counter as user approaches max length.
13. Warning (non-blocking) if chosen name duplicates another owner name.
14. "Reset to Google name" link in the dialog for reverting to the Google account name.

### Consistency patterns to follow

| Pattern | Existing Example | Profile Dialog |
|---|---|---|
| Modal overlay + centered modal | `CreateItemModal` (`.modal-overlay` + `.modal`) | Same CSS classes |
| `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal` | `CardDetail` (line 145-146) | Yes |
| Focus trap | `useFocusTrap` hook in `CardDetail` | Yes |
| Focus return on close | `CardDetail` close callback (lines 28-39) | Return to header trigger |
| Close on overlay click | `CreateItemModal` (line 44), `CardDetail` (line 148) | Yes |
| Escape to close | `useFocusTrap` handles this | Yes |
| Close button `aria-label` | `CardDetail` (line 155): `aria-label="Close"` | Yes |
| Form labels with `for`/`id` | `CreateItemModal` (lines 55-64) | Yes |
| Toast on success | `showToast("Item created")` pattern | "Display name updated" |
| Inline error styling | `.label-form-error` in `global.css` (line 1132) | Reuse for validation |

## Technical Notes
- **Files likely affected:**
  - `frontend/src/components/layout/app-header.tsx` -- add profile trigger button (currently a passive `<div>` in `kanban-board.tsx` lines 93-99; may need to extract to header component)
  - `frontend/src/components/profile/profile-dialog.tsx` -- new dialog component
  - `frontend/src/state/actions.ts` -- new `updateDisplayName` action (call `upsertOwner` + cascade item updates)
  - `frontend/src/api/sheets.ts` -- may need a batch update for cascading owner renames across Items
  - `frontend/src/components/board/kanban-board.tsx` -- update header section to use new profile trigger
  - `frontend/src/demo/mock-api.ts` -- mock profile update for demo mode
  - `frontend/src/global.css` -- profile trigger and dialog styles
- **Complexity:** medium (new dialog component + cascade rename logic + accessibility)
- **Rules sync required:** no (display name is not a business rule -- it is a data/UI concern)
- **Dependencies:** none -- `upsertOwner` already exists in `sheets.ts`
- **Patterns to follow:** `CreateItemModal` for modal overlay/structure, `CardDetail` for `useFocusTrap` and focus return, `cascadeLabelUpdate` pattern in `actions.ts` for the owner name cascade

## Open Questions
- None -- storage decision resolved (use existing Owners sheet `name` column via `upsertOwner`)

## Summary
Filter the Done column to show only items completed within the last 7 days, and add a completed-items archive dialog accessible from the Done column header for viewing and searching all completed items.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1: Done column filters to last 7 days
- **Given** items exist with status "Done", some completed within the last 7 days and some older
- **When** the board is displayed
- **Then** only items with `completed_at` within the last 7 calendar days appear in the Done column
- **And** items with no `completed_at` value or older than 7 days are hidden from the column

### AC2: Done column header shows archive link with count
- **Given** completed items older than 7 days exist
- **When** the board is displayed
- **Then** the Done column header shows a "View all N completed" link (font-size 12px, secondary text color) beneath the heading row, where N is the total count of all Done items
- **And** if no archived items exist (all Done items are within 7 days), the link is not shown

### AC3: Archive dialog displays all completed items with proper accessibility
- **Given** the user clicks "View all N completed" in the Done column header
- **When** the archive dialog opens
- **Then** all items with status "Done" are displayed, sorted by `completed_at` descending (most recent first)
- **And** each item shows its title, owner, labels, and a human-readable completed date (e.g., "Completed 12 days ago" or "Completed Feb 27")
- **And** the dialog uses `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and `aria-label="Completed items archive"`
- **And** focus moves to the search input on open, and returns to the "View all" trigger button on close
- **And** the dialog uses the `useFocusTrap` hook for keyboard navigation (Tab cycling, Escape to close)
- **And** the dialog can be closed with a close button, Escape key, or clicking outside
- **And** the search field stays fixed at the top while the item list scrolls independently

### AC4: Archive dialog supports text search with clear button
- **Given** the archive dialog is open with completed items displayed
- **When** the user types in the search field
- **Then** items are filtered in real time by case-insensitive title match
- **And** the search input has `aria-label="Search completed items"`
- **And** a visible results count is shown with `aria-live="polite"` so screen readers announce changes
- **And** a clear ("×") button appears inside the search field when text is present
- **And** clearing the search field (via clear button or manual deletion) restores the full list
- **And** when no items match, a "No matching items" empty state is shown

### AC5: Archive items can be opened for editing
- **Given** the archive dialog is open
- **When** the user clicks on an archived item
- **Then** the card detail panel opens (same as clicking any board card)
- **And** the user can change the status back to "To Do" or "In Progress" to reopen it
- **And** each archive item row has a minimum tap target of 44×44px for mobile accessibility

## Scope

### In Scope
- Date-based filtering of the Done column (7-day fixed window)
- "View all N completed" link in Done column header when archived items exist
- Modal/dialog for the archive view with full ARIA compliance
- Text search with clear button within the archive dialog (title only)
- Sticky search field with scrollable item list
- Clicking archive items opens the existing card detail panel
- Demo mode support (add an extra recent Done item for clear testing)
- Focus management (focus trap, return focus on close)

### Out of Scope
- Configurable time window (hardcoded to 7 days)
- Separate page/route for archive (use dialog to avoid adding routing)
- Advanced filters in archive (owner, label, date range) — future enhancement
- Permanent deletion or hard archive of items
- Apps Script backend changes (filtering happens client-side)
- List view changes (archive applies to board view only; list view already shows all)
- Keyboard shortcut to open archive (deferred to future enhancement)

## Technical Notes
- **Files likely affected:**
  - `frontend/src/state/board-store.ts` — add `recentDoneItems` and `archivedDoneItems` computed signals
  - `frontend/src/components/board/kanban-board.tsx` — pass filtered Done items to column, render archive dialog
  - `frontend/src/components/board/column.tsx` — add "View all N completed" link for Done column
  - `frontend/src/components/archive/` — new archive dialog component (follow ProfileDialog pattern for ARIA)
  - `frontend/src/components/board/card-detail.tsx` — no changes expected (reuse as-is)
  - `frontend/src/demo/mock-data.ts` — add one more recent Done item for testing
  - `frontend/tests/` — new tests for date filtering, archive dialog, search, and accessibility
- **Complexity:** medium (new dialog component + state changes, but straightforward logic)
- **Rules sync required:** no (no business rule changes, just UI filtering)
- **Dependencies:** none — `completed_at` field already exists and is populated correctly
- **Key implementation detail:** Use `completed_at` timestamp for the 7-day filter. Compare against `Date.now() - 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`. Follow ProfileDialog pattern for dialog accessibility.

## Open Questions
None — all questions resolved. UX review incorporated.

## Summary
Add individual sub-task deletion with confirmation, an owner picker during sub-task creation, and up/down reorder controls for sub-tasks within the card detail panel.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1: Delete a sub-task individually
- **Given** a parent item is open in the card detail panel and it has sub-tasks
- **When** the user hovers over a sub-task row (desktop) or views the row (mobile/tablet)
- **Then** a delete button (× icon) appears on that row
- **When** the user clicks the delete button
- **Then** a browser `confirm()` dialog appears ("Delete sub-task '{title}'?")
- **When** the user confirms
- **Then** the sub-task is removed from the sheet, an audit log entry is written, and the sub-task list updates immediately (optimistic UI)

### AC2: Delete sub-task cancellation
- **Given** the delete confirmation dialog is showing for a sub-task
- **When** the user clicks Cancel
- **Then** no deletion occurs and the sub-task remains unchanged

### AC3: Assign owner during sub-task creation
- **Given** the user is adding a new sub-task via the inline input
- **When** the sub-task creation row is visible
- **Then** an owner dropdown appears next to the title input, defaulting to the parent item's owner
- **When** the user tabs from the title input to the owner dropdown, or clicks the owner dropdown
- **Then** the creation row remains open (does not cancel on blur between sibling controls)
- **When** the user submits the sub-task (Enter key or blur away from the entire creation row)
- **Then** the new sub-task is created with the selected owner

### AC4: Reorder sub-tasks with up/down controls
- **Given** a parent item has 2 or more sub-tasks
- **When** the user hovers over a sub-task row (desktop) or views the row (mobile/tablet)
- **Then** up and down arrow buttons appear
- **Then** the first item's up button and the last item's down button are visually disabled (`opacity: 0.3`, `aria-disabled="true"`) rather than hidden, so layout doesn't shift
- **When** the user clicks an enabled arrow button
- **Then** the sub-task swaps `sort_order` with its neighbor, the list re-renders in the new order, and the updated sort orders are persisted to the sheet

### AC5: Single sub-task has no reorder controls
- **Given** a parent item has exactly 1 sub-task
- **When** the user views the sub-task list
- **Then** no up/down arrow buttons are shown (nothing to reorder)

### AC6: Keyboard and touch accessibility
- **Given** a sub-task row receives keyboard focus (`:focus-within`)
- **Then** the action buttons (delete, reorder) are revealed, same as hover
- **Given** the user is on a touch device (mobile/tablet, `max-width: 768px`)
- **Then** action buttons are always visible (no hover required)
- **Then** all interactive elements in the sub-task row have a minimum touch target of 44x44px
- **Then** all icon-only buttons have descriptive `aria-label` attributes (e.g., "Move up", "Move down", "Delete sub-task")

## Scope

### In Scope
- Delete button per sub-task row with browser `confirm()` dialog
- Owner dropdown in the sub-task creation row (reuse existing `<select>` pattern)
- Up/down arrow buttons for reordering (swap adjacent sort_order values)
- Optimistic UI for all three actions
- Audit log entries for delete and reorder actions
- Hover-reveal on desktop, always-visible on mobile/tablet (`max-width: 768px`)
- `:focus-within` reveals action buttons for keyboard users
- Disabled arrow styling at list boundaries (opacity + `aria-disabled`)
- Focus-container pattern on creation row to prevent premature blur cancellation

### Out of Scope
- Drag-and-drop reordering for sub-tasks (keep it simple with arrows)
- Bulk delete or multi-select for sub-tasks
- Swipe-to-delete gesture
- Inline confirmation UI (using browser `confirm()` for simplicity and consistency)
- Reorder animation (nice-to-have follow-up)

## Technical Notes
- **Files likely affected:**
  - `frontend/src/components/board/card-detail.tsx` — add delete button, owner picker on create, reorder arrows, focus-container logic for creation row
  - `frontend/src/state/actions.ts` — `deleteItem()` already works for individual items; add a `reorderSubtasks()` action that swaps sort_order values and persists
  - `frontend/src/global.css` — styles for action buttons (hover/focus-within reveal on desktop, always-visible on mobile), 44px touch targets on mobile, disabled arrow state
- **Complexity:** medium (3 files, moderate UI logic for reorder swap + responsive action visibility)
- **Rules sync required:** no — no new business rules, just UI + CRUD operations
- **Dependencies:** none — all required APIs (delete row, update row) already exist
- **Existing patterns to reuse:**
  - `deleteItem()` in actions.ts handles single-item delete + audit log
  - `<select>` owner dropdown already used for existing sub-task owner changes
  - `bySortOrder` comparator already sorts sub-tasks correctly
  - Optimistic UI pattern used throughout actions.ts
  - Parent item delete already uses `confirm()` — same pattern here
- **UX implementation guidance:**
  - Action buttons (×, ▲, ▼) grouped on the right of each sub-task row, after the owner dropdown
  - Desktop: hidden by default, shown on `.subtask-item:hover` and `.subtask-item:focus-within`
  - Mobile (`max-width: 768px`): always visible
  - Sub-task row min-height: 36px desktop, 44px mobile
  - Creation row: replace `onBlur={cancelSubtask}` on the input with a `onFocusOut` handler on the container that checks `e.relatedTarget` — only cancel when focus leaves the entire creation row (title input + owner dropdown)
  - Disabled arrows: `opacity: 0.3; cursor: not-allowed; aria-disabled="true"` (don't hide, to prevent layout shift)

## Summary

Add a dev/demo mode that bypasses Google OAuth and loads static mock board data when running on localhost, so QA and UX agents can visually test the app via preview tools without requiring real authentication. Write operations (drag, edit, create, delete) work against in-memory state only and do not persist.

## Context

The QA and UX agents use preview tools (preview_screenshot, preview_click, preview_inspect, preview_resize) to visually verify the running app. Currently, the preview server shows the Google Sign-in page and agents cannot proceed past it — blocking all visual/functional testing.

Automated tests (vitest) work fine since they mock the API layer, but real browser-based verification is impossible without auth.

## Activation

Demo mode uses **defense in depth** — both conditions must be true:
1. The Vite env var `VITE_DEMO_MODE=true` must be set at build time
2. The query parameter `?demo=true` must be present in the URL

This means:
- Production builds on GitHub Pages never set `VITE_DEMO_MODE`, so `?demo=true` alone does nothing
- Local dev builds with `VITE_DEMO_MODE=true` still require the query param, so devs don't accidentally run in demo mode
- Agents activate it by navigating to `http://localhost:5173/hive/?demo=true`

## Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1: Demo mode activates with both env var and query param

```gherkin
Given the app is built with VITE_DEMO_MODE=true
  And the user navigates to http://localhost:5173/hive/?demo=true
When the page loads
Then the Google OAuth flow is bypassed entirely
  And a mock user (name: "Demo User", email: "demo@hive.local") is injected into auth context
  And the board renders with mock data (no loading spinner shown for more than 500ms)
  And a visible "Demo Mode" banner or badge is displayed in the header
```

### Scenario 2: Demo mode does NOT activate on production (GitHub Pages)

```gherkin
Given the app is deployed to GitHub Pages (VITE_DEMO_MODE is not set)
When a user navigates to https://luketmoss.github.io/hive/?demo=true
Then demo mode is NOT active
  And the normal Google Sign-in screen is shown
  And no mock data is loaded
```

### Scenario 3: Demo mode does NOT activate without query param

```gherkin
Given the app is built with VITE_DEMO_MODE=true
When the user navigates to http://localhost:5173/hive/ (no ?demo=true)
Then demo mode is NOT active
  And the normal Google Sign-in screen is shown
```

### Scenario 4: Mock data covers all board features

```gherkin
Given demo mode is active
When the board finishes loading
Then the Items data includes at least:
  - 2+ items in "To Do" column
  - 2+ items in "In Progress" column (each with an owner assigned)
  - 1+ items in "Done" column (with completed_at set)
  - 1+ item with sub-tasks (parent_id relationships)
  - 1+ item with a due date in the past (renders as overdue)
  - 1+ item with a scheduled date
  - Items with labels assigned
And the Owners data includes at least 2 owners
And the Labels data includes at least 3 labels with distinct colors
And all data is static/deterministic (same data every load, for reproducible test screenshots)
```

### Scenario 5: Write operations work in-memory only

```gherkin
Given demo mode is active
  And the board is loaded with mock data
When the user drags a card from "To Do" to "In Progress"
Then the card moves to "In Progress" in the UI
  And no HTTP requests are made to the Google Sheets API
  And business rules still apply (e.g., owner required for In Progress)
When the user creates a new item via the + button
Then the item appears on the board
  And no HTTP requests are made to the Google Sheets API
When the user edits a card's title or description
Then the change is reflected in the UI
  And no HTTP requests are made to the Google Sheets API
When the page is refreshed
Then the board resets to the original mock data (changes are not persisted)
```

## Scope

### In Scope
- `isDemoMode()` utility function checking both env var and query param
- `DemoAuthProvider` component that wraps `AuthProvider` and injects mock auth state when demo is active
- Static mock data module (`frontend/src/demo/mock-data.ts`) with realistic Items, Owners, and Labels
- Mock Sheets API layer (`frontend/src/demo/mock-api.ts`) that reads/writes to in-memory signals instead of HTTP
- Demo mode banner/badge in the board header
- `VITE_DEMO_MODE` added to `env.d.ts` type declarations and `.env.example`
- 30-second polling disabled in demo mode (no point refreshing static data)

### Out of Scope
- Apps Script changes (demo mode is frontend-only)
- Randomized or seeded data generation — mock data is a static constant
- Demo mode behind a feature flag service — env var + query param is sufficient
- E2E test suite using demo mode (that is a separate issue)
- Mocking the Audit Log tab — audit entries are fire-and-forget and not displayed

## Technical Notes

### Affected Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `frontend/src/env.d.ts` | Add `VITE_DEMO_MODE` to `ImportMetaEnv` |
| `frontend/.env.example` | Add `VITE_DEMO_MODE=` |
| `frontend/src/demo/mock-data.ts` | **New** — static mock Items, Owners, Labels |
| `frontend/src/demo/mock-api.ts` | **New** — in-memory implementations of `fetchAllItems`, `fetchOwners`, `fetchLabels`, `createItemRow`, `updateItemRow`, `deleteItemRow`, `appendAuditEntry` |
| `frontend/src/demo/demo-utils.ts` | **New** — `isDemoMode()` helper |
| `frontend/src/auth/auth-provider.tsx` | Detect demo mode early; if active, skip GIS init and provide mock token/user |
| `frontend/src/state/actions.ts` | Import demo API functions conditionally; swap `sheets.*` calls for `mock-api.*` calls when `isDemoMode()` is true |
| `frontend/src/app.tsx` | Disable 30s polling interval when demo mode is active |
| `frontend/src/components/board/kanban-board.tsx` | Show "Demo Mode" banner in header when `isDemoMode()` |
| `frontend/index.html` | Conditionally skip GIS `<script>` tag in demo mode (or let it fail silently) |

### Complexity

**Medium.** The main work is:
1. Creating the mock data with realistic coverage (~50 lines)
2. Building the mock API layer that mirrors `sheets.ts` signatures but uses signals (~60 lines)
3. Wiring the demo detection into auth-provider and actions (~30 lines of conditional logic)
4. The GIS script in `index.html` loads async and can be left as-is — `auth-provider.tsx` short-circuits before it's used

### Implementation Approach

The cleanest pattern is to make `actions.ts` import from either `../api/sheets` or `../demo/mock-api` based on `isDemoMode()`. Since Vite tree-shakes dead code, the mock module won't be included in production builds where `VITE_DEMO_MODE` is not set. The auth provider can check `isDemoMode()` at the top of its `useEffect` and immediately call `setToken('demo-token')` / `setUser(demoUser)` without initializing the GIS client.

## Open Questions — Resolved

| Question | Decision |
|----------|----------|
| Query param vs env var? | **Both** — defense in depth. Env var (`VITE_DEMO_MODE=true`) gates the feature at build time; query param (`?demo=true`) activates it at runtime. |
| Static or randomized mock data? | **Static.** Deterministic data ensures reproducible screenshots for agent testing. |
| Read-only or read-write in demo mode? | **Read-write (in-memory).** Write operations update signals but never call the Sheets API. This lets agents test the full UX flow including drag-and-drop and form submission. |

## Summary

Due Date and Scheduled Date need clearer visual distinction on the card preview in the board view. Currently, the scheduled date shows a generic calendar emoji and the due date shows no icon at all -- just a bare date string. At a glance on small cards, users cannot quickly tell which date is which.

## Current Behavior

- **Scheduled date** renders as: calendar emoji + date via `.card-scheduled`
- **Due date** renders as: bare date, no icon/label via `.card-due`
- When overdue, due date gains red color + `(overdue)` suffix, but there is no visual differentiation when the date is not yet overdue
- Neither date has a text label, making them hard to distinguish

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1: Due date displays with a text label and distinct deadline icon
**Given** an item has a `due_date` set and is not overdue
**When** the card renders on the board
**Then** the due date displays as "Due: Mar 20" with a short text label prefix
**And** optionally includes an alarm icon before the label
**And** it retains the existing `.card-due` CSS class

### AC2: Scheduled date displays with a text label and calendar icon
**Given** an item has a `scheduled_date` set
**When** the card renders on the board
**Then** the scheduled date displays as "Sched: Mar 15" with a short text label prefix
**And** optionally includes a calendar icon before the label
**And** it retains the existing `.card-scheduled` CSS class

### AC3: Both dates are visually distinguishable when displayed together
**Given** an item has both `due_date` and `scheduled_date` set
**When** the card renders on the board
**Then** both dates are visible in the `.card-meta` row on the same flex row
**And** each date has a different text label ("Due:" vs "Sched:") and optionally a different icon prefix
**And** the due date text color uses `var(--color-text)` (darker, more prominent) while scheduled date keeps `var(--color-text-secondary)` (lighter)

### AC4: Overdue due date retains existing overdue styling
**Given** an item has a `due_date` in the past and status is not "Done"
**When** the card renders on the board
**Then** the due date shows the "Due:" label, red color via `.card-due-overdue`, and the `(overdue)` suffix (preserving all existing overdue behavior)

### AC5: Only set dates are displayed
**Given** an item where `due_date` is empty and `scheduled_date` is empty
**When** the card renders on the board
**Then** neither date element is rendered (no empty date placeholders)

**Given** an item where only `due_date` is set (no `scheduled_date`)
**When** the card renders on the board
**Then** only the due date with "Due:" label is shown; no scheduled date element is rendered

**Given** an item where only `scheduled_date` is set (no `due_date`)
**When** the card renders on the board
**Then** only the scheduled date with "Sched:" label is shown; no due date element is rendered

### AC6: Due date is more visually prominent than scheduled date
**Given** an item has both dates set and neither is overdue
**When** the card renders on the board
**Then** the due date text uses `font-weight: 600` and `color: var(--color-text)` to appear bolder/darker (the more actionable deadline gets more visual weight)
**And** the scheduled date text retains normal weight and `color: var(--color-text-secondary)` (secondary/lighter)

### AC7: Dates remain legible at small card widths
**Given** the board is viewed on a mobile device or narrow viewport (< 768px)
**When** a card displays one or both dates
**Then** the date text does not overflow or get clipped
**And** the labels and date text remain on a single line per date (via `white-space: nowrap` on both classes)
**And** the abbreviated labels ("Due:", "Sched:") add only ~40px each, keeping the layout compact

### AC8: Date elements have accessible aria-labels for screen readers
**Given** an item has a `scheduled_date` and/or `due_date` set
**When** the card renders on the board
**Then** the scheduled date element includes `aria-label="Scheduled date: Mar 15"` (using the full word, not the abbreviated "Sched:" visible label)
**And** the due date element includes `aria-label="Due date: Mar 20"` when not overdue
**And** the due date element includes `aria-label="Due date: Mar 20, overdue"` when the item is overdue
**And** this satisfies WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) for screen reader clarity

## Scope

### In Scope
- Add "Due:" text label prefix to the due date display in `card.tsx`
- Change scheduled date prefix from bare emoji to "Sched:" text label in `card.tsx`
- Optionally retain emoji icons alongside text labels
- Add `aria-label` attributes to both date span elements for screen reader accessibility
- Add `font-weight: 600` and darker text color to `.card-due` in `global.css` for non-overdue state
- Ensure `.card-due` has `white-space: nowrap` (matching `.card-scheduled`)
- Update existing card tests in `card.test.tsx` to verify text labels and aria-labels
- Verify existing overdue styling still works with the new labels

### Out of Scope
- Changes to the card-detail panel (dates are already clearly labeled there)
- Changes to the list view (uses the same Card component, so changes propagate automatically)
- Custom SVG icons (emoji icons are optional alongside text labels)
- Tooltip or hover behavior for dates
- Date formatting changes (keep existing "Mon DD" format)
- Relying on color alone to differentiate dates (WCAG 1.4.1 -- text labels provide the primary distinction)

## Technical Notes

### Files to modify
1. **`frontend/src/components/board/card.tsx`** (lines 93-101)
   - Change scheduled date to include "Sched:" text label prefix
   - Change due date to include "Due:" text label prefix
   - Add `aria-label` attributes to both date span elements:
     - Scheduled: `aria-label="Scheduled date: {formatted date}"`
     - Due (not overdue): `aria-label="Due date: {formatted date}"`
     - Due (overdue): `aria-label="Due date: {formatted date}, overdue"`

2. **`frontend/src/global.css`** (around line 360-367)
   - Update `.card-due` rule: `white-space: nowrap; font-weight: 600; color: var(--color-text);`
   - The `.card-due-overdue` rule already overrides color to `var(--color-overdue)` and sets `font-weight: 600`, so it will naturally take precedence for overdue items

3. **`frontend/src/components/board/card.test.tsx`**
   - Update tests to verify "Due:" and "Sched:" text labels are present in date text content
   - Add tests for `aria-label` attributes on date elements (AC8)
   - Add a test that both dates render with different text labels
   - Existing overdue tests should continue to pass with minor updates for new label format

### Existing patterns to preserve
- The `parseLocalDate()` and `formatDate()` helper functions remain unchanged
- The `isOverdue` boolean logic remains unchanged
- The `.card-due-overdue` CSS class toggling remains unchanged
- The `Card` component interface (`Props`) remains unchanged

### UX rationale
- **Text labels over icons alone**: The UX review found that short text labels ("Due:", "Sched:") are universally understood and do not rely on color or icon rendering. This is the single most effective change for date distinguishability.
- **Visual hierarchy**: Due date gets `font-weight: 600` because it is the more actionable deadline.
- **Accessibility**: `aria-label` attributes satisfy WCAG 4.1.2 and provide full context to screen readers (using unabbreviated "Scheduled date" / "Due date" rather than the abbreviated visual labels).
- **What to avoid**: Do not rely on color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). Do not hide dates behind hover/tooltip.

### Testing approach
- All existing tests in `card.test.tsx` and `card-mobile.test.tsx` must continue to pass
- Tests that assert on `.card-due` or `.card-scheduled` text content will need updates to account for "Due:" and "Sched:" label prefixes
- New tests needed for `aria-label` attribute values (including overdue variant)
- Run `cd frontend && npm test` to verify

## Summary
The owner dropdown should be populated from users who have access to Hive, showing display names (not emails). When a new user signs in for the first time, their Google display name and email should be automatically added to the Owners sheet so they immediately appear in owner dropdowns.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1: First-time sign-in auto-registers owner
**Given** a user signs into Hive for the first time (their Google email is not yet in the Owners sheet)
**When** the board finishes loading
**Then** a new row is appended to the Owners sheet with their Google display name and email
**And** the owner list in the UI refreshes to include the new name

### Scenario 2: Returning user does not duplicate
**Given** a user whose Google email already exists in the Owners sheet signs in
**When** the board finishes loading
**Then** no duplicate row is created in the Owners sheet
**And** if their Google display name has changed, the name in the Owners sheet is updated to match

### Scenario 3: Owner dropdown shows display names
**Given** the Owners sheet contains entries with display names
**When** the user opens the owner dropdown (in Create Item modal, Card Detail panel, or Filter Bar)
**Then** each option shows the display name (e.g., "Luke", "Sarah"), not the email address
**And** an "Unassigned" option remains as the first/default choice

### Scenario 4: Existing items continue to display correctly
**Given** existing items already have an `owner` field set to a display name (e.g., "Mom")
**When** the board renders those items
**Then** the owner name displays correctly on cards and in the detail panel
**And** no migration of existing data is required (names in the Owners sheet are already display names)

### Scenario 5: Auto-register fails gracefully
**Given** a user signs in but the Sheets API call to append/update the Owners row fails (e.g., network error)
**When** the auto-register attempt fails
**Then** the board still loads successfully with the existing owner list
**And** a non-blocking error is logged to the console (no toast error shown to the user)

## Scope

### In scope
- Auto-register: after OAuth sign-in, check if the signed-in user's email exists in the Owners sheet; if not, append a new row with `(display_name, email)`; if yes but name differs, update the name
- Frontend: new `ensureOwnerRegistered(user, token)` function called during board load
- Sheets API: new `upsertOwner(name, email, token)` function in `frontend/src/api/sheets.ts`
- Refresh the `owners` signal after upsert so the UI reflects the new entry
- Demo mode: skip auto-registration (mock data already has owners)

### Out of scope
- Self-service user management / invite flow
- Removing users from the Owners sheet (remains a manual process)
- Changing how items reference owners (items still store the display name string)
- Apps Script changes (the Apps Script `getOwners()` already reads both columns; no backend changes needed)
- Avatar/profile picture display
- Handling Google accounts with no display name set (edge case — fall back to email prefix)

## Technical Notes

### Files likely to change
1. **`frontend/src/api/sheets.ts`** — Add `upsertOwner(name: string, email: string, token: string)` function that reads Owners sheet, checks for existing email, appends or updates accordingly
2. **`frontend/src/state/actions.ts`** — Add `ensureOwnerRegistered(user: UserInfo, token: string)` called inside `loadBoard()` after auth, before or after the parallel data fetch
3. **`frontend/src/api/types.ts`** — No changes needed (Owner type already has `name` and `google_account`)
4. **`frontend/src/demo/mock-data.ts`** — No changes needed

### Implementation approach
- In `loadBoard()` (actions.ts), after the token is available and `user` info is known, call `ensureOwnerRegistered(user, token)`
- `ensureOwnerRegistered` should:
  1. Fetch the current Owners sheet rows
  2. Look for a row where column B (google_account) matches `user.email`
  3. If not found: append a new row `[user.name, user.email]`
  4. If found but name differs: update the existing row's name column
  5. Re-fetch owners into the signal so the UI updates
- The `loadBoard` function currently fetches owners in parallel with items and labels. The upsert should happen before or after that parallel fetch, then re-fetch owners if a write occurred.
- Gate on `isDemoMode()` — skip in demo mode.

### Business rules sync
- No changes to `rules.ts` or `rules.js` — the owner field on items is still a plain display name string.

### Estimated complexity
**Small** — 2 files changed (sheets.ts, actions.ts), straightforward read-then-write logic against the Owners sheet. No new UI components, no business rule changes.

### Dependencies
- Requires the signed-in user's `name` and `email` from Google OAuth (already available via `useAuth()` / `UserInfo`)
- Requires write access to the Owners sheet (the OAuth scope `spreadsheets` already grants this)

## Summary

Record the authenticated Google user who created each item on the kanban board. Store the creator's email address in a new `created_by` column on the Items sheet and display it in the card detail view.

## Motivation

With multiple family members using the board, knowing who created an item provides useful context — especially for items that are unassigned or reassigned. The app already has user identity via Google Identity Services (email, name, picture) but does not persist it on items.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1: New column in Items sheet
- **Given** the Items Google Sheet currently has 13 columns (A:M)
- **When** this feature is implemented
- **Then** a new column N "CreatedBy" is added to the Items sheet header row
- **And** the column stores the creator's Google email address (e.g. `mom@family.com`)

### AC2: Frontend captures creator on item creation
- **Given** a user is authenticated and creates a new item via the Create Item modal
- **When** the item is written to the sheet
- **Then** the `created_by` field is populated with the authenticated user's email address
- **And** the field is included in the row appended to `Items!A:N`

### AC3: Apps Script captures creator on item creation
- **Given** a caller invokes the `createItem` action via the Apps Script API
- **When** `data.created_by` is provided in the payload
- **Then** the value is stored in the CreatedBy column
- **And** if `data.created_by` is omitted, the field defaults to the `actor` value (backward compatible)

### AC4: Creator displayed in card detail view
- **Given** a user opens the card detail panel for an item that has a `created_by` value
- **When** the detail panel renders
- **Then** a "Created by" line is displayed in the metadata section (alongside Created/Updated/Completed timestamps)
- **And** the display shows the creator's display name if the email matches a known owner, otherwise shows the raw email

### AC5: Creator field is read-only
- **Given** a user opens the card detail panel
- **When** viewing the "Created by" metadata
- **Then** the field is not editable (it is set once at creation time and never changed)

### AC6: Existing items without creator display gracefully
- **Given** an item was created before this feature was implemented (no `created_by` value)
- **When** the card detail panel is opened
- **Then** the "Created by" line either shows "Unknown" or is hidden entirely (no errors or blank text)

### AC7: Demo mode includes created_by data
- **Given** the app is running in demo mode
- **When** mock items are loaded
- **Then** each mock item has a plausible `created_by` email matching its owner's `google_account`

## Scope

### In Scope
- New `CreatedBy` column (column N) in the Items sheet
- `created_by` field added to the `Item` TypeScript interface and Apps Script column mapping
- Frontend `createItem` action passes `user.email` as `created_by`
- Apps Script `createItem` function stores `created_by` from payload
- Card detail view displays creator in metadata section
- Resolve email to display name using Owners list
- Column range updates (`A:M` -> `A:N`, `A2:M` -> `A2:N`)
- Mock data updated with `created_by` values
- Unit test updates for new field

### Out of Scope
- Displaying creator on the card summary (board/list view) — card is already dense
- Backfilling `created_by` for existing items — they will show "Unknown" or be hidden
- Tracking "last modified by" — separate concern, separate issue
- Creator-based filtering or sorting — can be a follow-up
- Changing the audit log `actor` field (it already captures who performed each action)

## Open Questions — Resolved

| Question | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Email, display name, or both? | Store email, display name for rendering | Email is unique and reliable as the stored identifier. The Owners table already maps email to name for UI display. |
| Backfill existing items? | No backfill — leave blank | Simpler, avoids guessing. Items show "Unknown" gracefully. |
| Card summary or detail view? | Detail view only | Card summary is already crowded with owner, dates, labels, subtask progress. |
| Track last modified by? | Out of scope | Different concern, merits its own issue. Audit log already tracks per-action actors. |

## Technical Notes

### Files to modify

**Frontend (7 files):**
1. `frontend/src/api/types.ts` — Add `created_by: string` to `Item` interface
2. `frontend/src/api/sheets.ts` — Update `rowToItem` (index 13), `itemToRow` (append field), all range references from `M` to `N` (fetchAllItems, createItemRow, updateItemRow)
3. `frontend/src/state/actions.ts` — Pass `user.email` (not `user.name`) as `created_by` when constructing the item in `createItem()`; signature change to accept email or pass `UserInfo`
4. `frontend/src/components/board/card-detail.tsx` — Add "Created by" line in `.detail-meta` section; resolve email to display name via `owners` signal
5. `frontend/src/components/forms/create-item-modal.tsx` — No changes needed (uses `createItem` action which handles it)
6. `frontend/src/demo/mock-data.ts` — Add `created_by` to every `MOCK_ITEMS` entry
7. `frontend/src/demo/mock-api.ts` — May need adjustment if `createItemRow` signature changes

**Apps Script (3 files):**
1. `apps-script/src/types.js` — Add `CREATED_BY: 13` to `COL`, update `ITEM_COLUMN_COUNT` from 13 to 14
2. `apps-script/src/utils.js` — Update `rowToItem` and `itemToRow` to include `created_by` at index 13
3. `apps-script/src/items.js` — In `createItem()`, read `data.created_by` (fall back to `actor`); add `created_by` to the constructed item object

### Data model change
```
Items sheet column N (index 13): "CreatedBy"
Type: string (email address)
Set on: creation only
Mutable: no
```

### Column range impact
All Sheets API calls referencing `Items!A:M` or `Items!A2:M` must be updated to `Items!A:N` / `Items!A2:N`. This affects:
- `fetchAllItems`: `Items!A2:M` -> `Items!A2:N`
- `createItemRow`: `Items!A:M` -> `Items!A:N`
- `updateItemRow`: `Items!A${row}:M${row}` -> `Items!A${row}:N${row}`

### Display name resolution
The Owners table maps `google_account` (email) to `name`. The card detail view should look up the creator's email in the owners list and display the name if found, otherwise fall back to the raw email. Example:
```typescript
const creatorName = owners.value.find(o => o.google_account === item.created_by)?.name || item.created_by || 'Unknown';
```

### No business rules sync needed
The `created_by` field has no impact on status transitions or validation logic. No changes needed in `frontend/src/state/rules.ts` or `apps-script/src/rules.js`.

## Complexity

**Small-medium.** This is a straightforward data model extension. The main work is updating column mappings and ranges consistently across both frontend and Apps Script layers. No new UI components, no new business rules, no architectural changes.

Estimated files changed: ~10  
Estimated effort: 2-3 hours

content.body: ## Summary Sub-tasks should be able to have owners independent of their parent item. The data model already supports this (each row in the Items sheet has its own `owner` column), but the frontend lacks a UI affordance to change a sub-task's owner after creation. ## Context Currently, when a sub-task is created via the card detail panel, it inherits the parent's owner automatically (`card-detail.tsx` line 78). This is the right default — less friction for the common case on a 2-person family board. However, once created, a sub-task's owner cannot be changed through the UI. Sub-tasks only appear as checkbox items within the parent's detail panel, showing title + owner label but no edit control. Sub-tasks are filtered out of board columns (`rootItems` filters `!parent_id`), so there's no way to open a sub-task's own detail panel to change its owner. **Example:** Mom creates "Grocery shopping" with sub-tasks. She wants to delegate "Pick up prescription" to Dad. Currently she has no way to reassign that sub-task from the UI. ## Resolved Questions - **Should sub-tasks default to parent's owner when created?** Yes — keep current behavior (less friction for the common case). - **Should there be a "cascade owner to all sub-tasks" option?** No — out of scope. Over-engineering for a 2-person family board. Owner changes on the parent should NOT automatically cascade to existing sub-tasks. ## Acceptance Criteria ### AC1: Sub-task owner is editable inline ```gherkin Given a parent item with sub-tasks is open in the detail panel When the user clicks on a sub-task's owner label (or the empty space where it would be) Then an owner dropdown appears inline for that sub-task And it contains "Unassigned" plus all owners from the Owners sheet ``` ### AC2: Selecting an owner saves immediately ```gherkin Given the owner dropdown is open on a sub-task When the user selects a different owner Then the sub-task's owner field is updated via the Sheets API And an audit log entry is written (field: "owner", old → new) And the dropdown closes, showing the new owner name ``` ### AC3: Sub-task creation still defaults to parent's owner ```gherkin Given a parent item owned by "Mom" When the user creates a new sub-task via "+ Add" Then the sub-task is created with owner = "Mom" And the owner label shows "Mom" on the new sub-task row ``` ### AC4: Sub-task can be set to "Unassigned" ```gherkin Given a sub-task with owner "Dad" When the user opens the owner dropdown and selects "Unassigned" Then the sub-task's owner is cleared (empty string) And the owner label area shows nothing (no "Unassigned" text in the subtask list) ``` ### AC5: Owner change respects "In Progress requires owner" rule ```gherkin Given a sub-task with status "In Progress" When the user tries to set the owner to "Unassigned" Then a toast error appears: "Cannot remove owner from In Progress items" And the owner is not changed ``` ### AC6: Changing parent's owner does NOT cascade to sub-tasks ```gherkin Given a parent item owned by "Mom" with sub-tasks owned by "Mom" and "Dad" When the user changes the parent's owner to "Dad" Then sub-task owners remain unchanged ("Mom" stays "Mom", "Dad" stays "Dad") ``` ### AC7: Apps Script API supports independent sub-task ownership ```gherkin Given a sub-task exists with owner "Mom" When an API call updates the sub-task's owner to "Dad" Then the owner is updated in the Items sheet And an audit entry is logged And the parent's owner is unchanged ``` ## Scope ### In Scope - Inline owner dropdown on each sub-task row in the detail panel - Owner dropdown populated from `owners` signal (same source as parent owner field) - Optimistic update + Sheets API write + audit log on owner change - Validation: prevent removing owner from "In Progress" sub-tasks - Existing tests updated/expanded for new sub-task owner editing ### Out of Scope - Cascade owner changes from parent to sub-tasks (explicitly excluded) - "Cascade owner to all sub-tasks" bulk action - Sub-task detail panel (opening a sub-task as its own full detail view) - Changing sub-task status to anything other than Done/To Do (toggle remains as-is) - Owner filtering affecting sub-task visibility within a parent card - Apps Script API changes (the API already supports `updateItem` with owner ## Summary

Add silent re-authentication when a cached OAuth token expires, both on page load and mid-session. Commit b1acb97 already implemented localStorage caching of the GIS token and user info. This issue covers the remaining gaps: gracefully handling token expiry during active use and attempting silent re-auth before forcing the user back to the login screen.

## Context

The current auth implementation (in `auth-provider.tsx`) caches the token in localStorage with a 60-second safety margin on the expiry. On page load, if the cached token is still within its expiry window, it is used directly -- no login screen, no network call. This works well for short-lived refreshes.

However, two gaps remain:

1. **Stale token on load**: If the cached token is technically within its expiry window but has been revoked server-side (e.g., user changed password, token revoked in Google security settings), the app loads into `AuthenticatedApp`, hits a 401 from the Sheets API, and shows a generic error toast. The user is stuck.

2. **Mid-session expiry**: GIS tokens last ~1 hour. If a user leaves the tab open and returns after the token expires, any Sheets API call (board refresh, item update, drag-and-drop) will fail with a 401. Currently nothing catches this to attempt re-auth -- it just shows "Failed to load board" or "Failed to update item" errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1: Cached token is valid on page load
```
Given the user previously signed in and a cached token exists in localStorage
  And the token has not expired (within the stored expiry window)
When the page loads
Then the app restores the session from cache without showing the login screen
  And the board loads using the cached token
  And no Google userinfo fetch is made (cached user info is used)
```
**Status: Already implemented (b1acb97). Included for completeness.**

### Scenario 2: Cached token fails on first API call (stale/revoked token)
```
Given a cached token exists in localStorage and appears valid (within expiry window)
  But the token has been revoked or is invalid server-side
When the app attempts to load the board and receives a 401 from the Sheets API
Then the app attempts silent re-auth via requestAccessToken({ prompt: '' })
  And if silent re-auth succeeds, the board loads with the new token
  And the new token and expiry are saved to localStorage
```

### Scenario 3: Silent re-auth fails after stale token
```
Given a cached token exists but is invalid server-side
  And silent re-auth via requestAccessToken({ prompt: '' }) fails or is dismissed
When the silent re-auth callback returns an error
Then the app clears the cached token from localStorage
  And the app shows the login screen
  And a toast message says "Session expired -- please sign in again"
```

### Scenario 4: Mid-session token expiry during a Sheets API call
```
Given the user is actively using the board
  And the OAuth token expires (after ~1 hour)
When any Sheets API call returns a 401 status
Then the app attempts silent re-auth via requestAccessToken({ prompt: '' })
  And if silent re-auth succeeds, the failed API call is retried with the new token
  And the user's work is not lost (optimistic updates remain in place)
```

### Scenario 5: Mid-session silent re-auth fails
```
Given the user is actively using the board and the token has expired
  And silent re-auth fails (user may have revoked consent, popup blocked, etc.)
When the re-auth callback returns an error
Then the app clears the cached token from localStorage
  And the app shows the login screen
  And a toast message says "Session expired -- please sign in again"
```

### Scenario 6: Explicit logout clears all cached state
```
Given the user is signed in with a cached token in localStorage
When the user clicks the logout button
Then the cached token, user info, and expiry are removed from localStorage
  And the user sees the login screen
  And no silent re-auth is attempted on next page load
```
**Status: Already implemented (b1acb97). Included for completeness.**

## Scope

### In scope
- **Silent re-auth on 401**: Intercept 401 responses from the Sheets API and attempt `requestAccessToken({ prompt: '' })` before surfacing errors
- **Retry failed API calls**: After successful silent re-auth, retry the original operation that triggered the 401
- **Toast on forced re-login**: Show "Session expired -- please sign in again" when silent re-auth fails and the user must re-authenticate manually
- **Loading state during re-auth**: While silent re-auth is in progress, do not flash the login screen -- keep showing the current board state or a subtle loading indicator
- **Unit tests**: Add tests for the auth provider caching, re-auth, and error handling logic

### Out of scope
- **Proactive token refresh before expiry** (e.g., refresh at the 50-minute mark) -- nice-to-have but not needed for a 2-user family app
- **Offline support or service worker caching** -- app is always-online by design
- **Migrating from localStorage to sessionStorage** -- localStorage was chosen in b1acb97 and is the right call for a family app where surviving tab close is more convenient
- **Caching board data in localStorage** -- only the auth token and user info are cached; board data is always fetched fresh
- **Changes to apps-script** -- this is purely a frontend auth flow change

## PM Decisions on Open Questions

1. **sessionStorage vs localStorage**: **localStorage** (already implemented). For a family app with only 2 users, surviving tab/browser close is more useful than the stricter sessionStorage scope. The token auto-expires after ~1 hour anyway, so the security risk is minimal.

2. **Cache user info in storage**: **Yes** (already implemented). The name, email, and picture are cached alongside the token. This avoids an extra userinfo fetch on every reload and makes the page-load experience instant.

3. **UX during validation on page load**: **Keep current behavior** -- the cached token is trusted optimistically on load. The user sees the board immediately (with a "Loading board..." spinner while Sheets data loads). If the token turns out to be stale, silent re-auth kicks in transparently. Only show the login screen if re-auth fails.

4. **Toast for failed re-auth**: **Yes**. Show "Session expired -- please sign in again" as an error toast when the user is forced back to the login screen. This gives clear feedback about why they are seeing the login screen again.

## Technical Notes

### Files likely to change
- **`frontend/src/auth/auth-provider.tsx`** -- Add a `reauth()` function that attempts silent token refresh. Expose it via context or as a callable the API layer can invoke on 401.
- **`frontend/src/api/sheets.ts`** -- Wrap the 401-throwing logic with a retry mechanism that calls `reauth()` before failing. Consider a wrapper/interceptor pattern (e.g., a `withReauth(apiCall)` higher-order function).
- **`frontend/src/auth/auth-context.tsx`** -- May need to expose a `reauth` method on the `AuthState` interface, or alternatively use a module-level callback pattern so the sheets API layer can trigger re-auth without being inside the React tree.
- **`frontend/src/state/actions.ts`** -- May need updates if the retry-on-401 pattern is implemented at the actions layer rather than the API layer.

### Architecture consideration
The main challenge is that `sheets.ts` is a plain module (not a component), so it cannot directly access React context. Two approaches:
1. **Module-level callback**: `auth-provider.tsx` registers a `reauth` callback on a shared module that `sheets.ts` can call. Simple, pragmatic.
2. **Actions layer retry**: Catch 401 in `actions.ts` (which has access to the token via function params), call reauth, and retry. Keeps sheets.ts pure but adds retry logic in multiple places.

Recommend approach #1 (module-level callback) for simplicity.

### Business rules sync
No changes needed to `frontend/src/state/rules.ts` or `apps-script/src/rules.js`. This is purely an auth/UX flow change.

### Estimated complexity
**Medium**. The localStorage caching is already done. The remaining work is:
- Building the 401-intercept + silent re-auth + retry mechanism (~60% of effort)
- Handling the edge cases (re-auth failure, clearing state, toast) (~20%)
- Tests (~20%)

Estimated effort: **3-5 hours** for an experienced developer familiar with GIS.

### Dependencies
- None. This is a self-contained frontend change.
- Requires a valid GIS client ID and an active Google session in the browser for silent re-auth to work (i.e., the user must still be logged into Google -- `prompt: ''` only skips the consent screen, it does not bypass Google login).

## Summary

Allow users to create, edit, and delete custom labels inline within the existing label picker (in Card Detail panel and Create Item modal). Labels are persisted to the Labels sheet (columns A-B: label name, hex color).

**Revised based on UX consultation.** Key design changes from the original spec:
- **Inline management** within the existing label picker instead of a standalone modal (the app has no settings area; inline is lower friction)
- **Preset color swatch palette** instead of free-form color picker (prevents poor accessibility choices, simpler on mobile)
- Accessibility improvements for new UI (aria-pressed, radiogroup for swatches, focus management, color name tooltips)

## Context

The Labels sheet and read-only label display already work end-to-end: cards show colored badges, the detail panel has a label picker, and the filter bar filters by label. However, labels are currently seeded manually in the sheet -- there is no way to create, rename, recolor, or delete labels from within the app.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1: Create a new label

**Given** the user is viewing the label picker (in Card Detail or Create Item modal)
**When** the user clicks a "+ New label" button at the end of the label picker row
**Then** an inline creation form expands below the label toggles containing: a text input for label name (auto-focused, max 30 characters, placeholder "Label name..."), a preset color swatch grid, and Save/Cancel buttons.

**When** the user enters a valid label name, selects a color swatch, and clicks Save (or presses Enter)
**Then** a new row is appended to the Labels sheet (columns A-B), the `labels` signal is refreshed, the new label appears in the label picker and can immediately be toggled onto the current item, and a success toast is shown.

### Scenario 2: Enter edit mode for existing labels

**Given** the user is viewing the label picker
**When** the user clicks a "Manage labels" toggle link/button below the picker
**Then** the picker enters "edit mode": each label toggle shows an edit (pencil) icon and a delete (trash) icon. The "Manage labels" toggle text changes to "Done" to exit edit mode.

**When** edit mode is active
**Then** label toggles do NOT toggle label assignment on/off (clicking the label itself has no effect in edit mode, only the edit/delete icons are actionable). This prevents accidental label changes while managing.

### Scenario 3: Edit an existing label (rename or recolor)

**Given** the user is in edit mode and clicks the edit icon on a label
**When** an inline edit form appears (replacing the label toggle) with the current name pre-filled and the current color pre-selected in the swatch grid
**Then** the user can change the name and/or color. On Save: the corresponding row in the Labels sheet is updated, the `labels` signal is refreshed, all cards currently displaying that label reflect the new name/color, and any items whose `labels` field contained the old name are updated to the new name (comma-separated string replacement in the Items sheet).

### Scenario 4: Delete a label

**Given** the user is in edit mode and clicks the delete icon on a label
**When** an inline confirmation appears (matching the existing delete-item pattern in CardDetail: "Remove label from all items?" with Cancel/Remove buttons)
**Then on confirm:** the label row is removed from the Labels sheet, the label is stripped from the `labels` field of all items that reference it (Items sheet update), the `labels` and `items` signals are refreshed, and a success toast is shown.
**Then on cancel:** the confirmation is dismissed, no changes are made.

### Scenario 5: Validation prevents duplicate or empty labels

**Given** the user is creating or renaming a label
**When** the user enters a name that is empty/whitespace-only OR matches an existing label name (case-insensitive)
**Then** the Save button is disabled and an inline validation message is shown (e.g. "Label name is required" or "A label with this name already exists").

### Scenario 6: Color selection via preset swatch grid

**Given** the user is in the label creation or edit form
**When** the color swatch grid is displayed
**Then** it shows 10-12 curated color swatches (including the 7 existing demo colors plus 3-5 additional ones). Each swatch is at least 32x32px. The first unused color is pre-selected for new labels; the current color is pre-selected for edits.

**Accessibility requirements for the swatch grid:**
- The grid uses `role="radiogroup"` with individual swatches as `role="radio"` and `aria-checked`.
- Arrow keys navigate between swatches (left/right/up/down).
- Each swatch has an `aria-label` with the color name (e.g., "Ocean Blue", "Forest Green") and shows the color name as a `title` tooltip for colorblind accessibility.
- Enter/Space selects a swatch.

### Scenario 7: Empty state when no labels exist

**Given** the board is loaded and there are no labels in the Labels sheet
**When** the label picker area is displayed (in Card Detail or Create Item modal)
**Then** a friendly message is shown: "No labels yet" with a prominent "+ Create label" button.

### Scenario 8: Label toggle accessibility (aria-pressed)

**Given** the label picker is in normal mode (not edit mode)
**When** label toggle buttons are rendered
**Then** each button has `aria-pressed="true"` or `aria-pressed="false"` reflecting whether the label is currently assigned to the item.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Inline label management UI within the existing label picker (create, edit, delete)
- "+ New label" button and inline creation form
- "Manage labels" edit mode toggle with per-label edit/delete controls
- Preset color swatch grid (10-12 curated colors) with `role="radiogroup"` keyboard navigation
- Frontend Sheets API functions: `createLabel`, `updateLabel`, `deleteLabel` in `sheets.ts`
- Cascade rename/delete: update the `labels` field on affected Items rows when a label is renamed or deleted
- Label name validation (non-empty, unique case-insensitive, max 30 chars)
- Mock API equivalents for demo mode
- Refresh `labels` signal after mutations
- Toast feedback on success/error
- `aria-pressed` on label toggle buttons (existing picker fix)
- Color name tooltips on swatches for colorblind users
- Empty state when no labels exist
- Focus management: auto-focus name input on create/edit, return focus to trigger on close/cancel

### Out of Scope
- Standalone label management modal or settings page (inline approach chosen instead)
- Free-form color picker / custom hex input (preset palette only; could add later)
- Touch target size fix for existing label toggles (pre-existing issue -- file as separate issue)
- Apps Script backend label CRUD (the frontend writes directly to Sheets; Apps Script `getLabels()` remains read-only for now)
- Label icons (colors only)
- Label ordering/sorting/drag-to-reorder
- Maximum label count enforcement (2-user family app -- not needed now)
- Permission/role checks for who can manage labels
- Audit log entries for label changes
- Undo toast for deletion (inline confirmation is sufficient)
- Keyboard shortcut (L) to open label picker

## Technical Notes

### Files to create or modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `frontend/src/api/sheets.ts` | Add `createLabel()`, `updateLabel()`, `deleteLabel()` functions using `sheetsAppend`, `sheetsUpdate`, `sheetsDeleteRow` for the Labels sheet. Add a helper to find the Labels sheet ID for row deletion. Also need a function to batch-update Items rows when a label is renamed or deleted. |
| `frontend/src/api/types.ts` | No changes needed -- `Label` interface already has `label` and `color` fields. |
| `frontend/src/state/actions.ts` | Add `createLabel()`, `updateLabel()`, `deleteLabel()` action functions that call the new sheets API, refresh the `labels` signal, handle cascading item updates, and show toasts. |
| `frontend/src/state/board-store.ts` | No new modal signal needed (inline approach). May add a `labelEditMode` signal if shared across components. |
| `frontend/src/components/labels/label-picker-manager.tsx` | **New file.** Wraps the label picker with management controls: "+ New label" button, "Manage labels" toggle, inline create/edit forms, color swatch grid. Used by both CardDetail and CreateItemModal. |
| `frontend/src/components/labels/color-swatch-grid.tsx` | **New file.** Accessible color swatch grid component with `role="radiogroup"`, arrow key navigation, color name labels. |
| `frontend/src/components/board/card-detail.tsx` | Replace inline label picker markup with the new `LabelPickerManager` component. Add `aria-pressed` to toggle buttons (handled inside new component). |
| `frontend/src/components/forms/create-item-modal.tsx` | Replace inline label picker markup with the new `LabelPickerManager` component. |
| `frontend/src/demo/mock-api.ts` | Add mock implementations of `createLabel`, `updateLabel`, `deleteLabel` for demo mode. |
| `frontend/src/global.css` | Add styles for inline management UI, color swatch grid, edit mode states, empty state. |

### Preset color palette

Include the 7 existing demo colors plus 3-5 additional swatches. Each color needs a human-readable name for the `aria-label` and tooltip. Example:

| Name | Hex | Usage |
|------|-----|-------|
| Tomato Red | #E74C3C | Urgent / important |
| Sunset Orange | #F39C12 | Warnings / attention |
| Sunflower Yellow | #F1C40F | Highlight |
| Emerald Green | #2ECC71 | Success / complete |
| Ocean Blue | #3498DB | Info / default |
| Royal Purple | #9B59B6 | Special |
| Slate Gray | #95A5A6 | Low priority |
| Hot Pink | #E91E63 | Fun / personal |
| Teal | #00BCD4 | Category |
| Brown | #795548 | Misc |

(Final palette may be adjusted during implementation to ensure visual distinction and WCAG contrast compliance.)

### Key implementation considerations

- **Inline approach:** The label picker in CardDetail and CreateItemModal both render `.label-picker` markup today. Extract this into a shared `LabelPickerManager` component that handles both normal (toggle) mode and edit mode, plus the creation form.
- **Cascade on rename:** When a label is renamed, scan all Items rows where the `labels` column contains the old name, replace it in the comma-separated string, and batch-update those rows.
- **Cascade on delete:** Same approach -- strip the deleted label from all Items that reference it.
- **Labels sheet ID:** The `deleteLabel` function will need the sheet ID (gid) of the Labels tab for `batchUpdate` row deletion, similar to how `deleteItemRow` discovers the Items sheet ID.
- **No rules sync needed:** Label CRUD does not involve business rules, so `apps-script/src/rules.js` and `frontend/src/state/rules.ts` do not need changes.
- **Optimistic updates:** Follow the existing pattern in `actions.ts` -- update the `labels` signal optimistically, then call the API, and rollback on failure.
- **Edit mode context:** In CreateItemModal, edit mode should still allow the user to see which labels they have selected (visual indication) even though toggling is disabled. This ensures they do not lose context while managing labels.

### Complexity estimate

**Medium.** The inline UI is slightly more complex than a standalone modal (managing two modes in one component) but avoids building a separate entry point. The color swatch grid with full keyboard navigation adds some implementation effort. The cascade logic for rename/delete across Items rows remains the main backend complexity. Estimate: 3-4 days of development effort.
