Add ARIA labels, roles, and semantic attributes to all interactive elements so screen readers can identify and describe them correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1: Filter bar selects have accessible labels
- **Given** the filter bar renders with owner, label, and group-by selects
- **When** a screen reader encounters each select
- **Then** each has an accessible name (via `aria-label` or associated `<label>`) describing its purpose: "Filter by owner", "Filter by label", "Group items by"

### AC2: FAB has accessible label
- **Given** the FAB button renders with a "+" text
- **When** a screen reader encounters the button
- **Then** it announces "Create new item" (via `aria-label`)

### AC3: Detail panel close button has accessible label
- **Given** the detail panel close button renders with an emoji
- **When** a screen reader encounters the button
- **Then** it announces "Close" (via `aria-label`)

### AC4: Columns have region roles
- **Given** the board renders with status columns
- **When** a screen reader encounters a column
- **Then** each column is identified as a region with a descriptive label (e.g., "To Do column, 3 items")

### AC5: Subtask checkboxes have accessible labels
- **Given** the detail panel shows subtask checkboxes
- **When** a screen reader encounters a checkbox
- **Then** it announces the subtask title (via `aria-label` linking checkbox to title text)

### AC6: Editable fields have accessible roles
- **Given** the detail panel shows click-to-edit fields (title, description)
- **When** a screen reader encounters the non-editing state
- **Then** the field is identified as interactive (via `role="button"` and descriptive `aria-label` like "Edit title")

## Scope

### In Scope
- `aria-label` on filter selects, FAB, close button
- `role="region"` with `aria-label` on columns
- `aria-label` on subtask checkboxes
- `role="button"` and `aria-label` on editable fields
- `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"` on detail panel overlay
- `role="status"` on toast component

### AC1: Scheduled date displays on card
- **Given** an item has a `scheduled_date` value set
- **When** the card renders on the board

- **Given** the detail panel is open

## Summary
Fix color contrast issues: label badges need automatic light/dark text based on background color, overdue dates need a non-color indicator, and column count badges need better contrast.

- **Given** a label badge renders with a background color from the Labels sheet
- **When** the background is light (e.g., yellow, light green)
- **Then** the text color is dark (e.g., black or dark gray) to meet WCAG 4.5:1 contrast ratio
- **And when** the background is dark (e.g., navy, dark red)
- **Then** the text color is white

- **Given** an item has a due date in the past and status is not Done

### AC3: Column count badge meets contrast requirements
- **Given** a column header renders with an item count badge
- **When** the badge appears on the column background color
- **Then** the text-to-background contrast ratio meets WCAG AA (4.5:1 for the 12px text)

### AC4: Label badge contrast works for all stored colors
- **Given** the Labels sheet contains various hex colors
- **When** label badges render across the board
- **Then** every badge has readable text regardless of the stored color (automatic calculation, not hardcoded per-label)

## Scope

### In Scope
- Luminance-based text color calculation for label badges
- Non-color overdue indicator on cards

## Summary

Display name changes in the profile dialog show a success toast but don't actually persist — reopening the profile reverts to the original Google account name. Board cards also don't reflect the updated name. The root cause is that the profile dialog reads `user.name` from the AuthContext (Google OAuth cache), which is never updated after a display name save. Additionally, the cascade rename uses this stale name as the "old" value, so items don't get updated either.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1: Display name persists across dialog open/close
- **Given** a signed-in user whose Owners-sheet display name is "Alice Smith"
- **When** the user opens the profile dialog, changes the name to "Alice", and clicks Save
- **Then** the dialog closes, and reopening it shows "Alice" (not "Alice Smith")

### AC2: Board header reflects updated display name
- **Given** the user has just saved a new display name "Alice"
- **When** the save completes
- **Then** the header user button shows "Alice" instead of the previous name

### AC3: Existing cards update to the new display name
- **Given** cards on the board are owned by the user (e.g., owner = "Alice Smith")
- **When** the user saves display name "Alice"
- **Then** all cards that had owner "Alice Smith" now show "Alice" — without a page refresh

### AC4: Persistence survives page reload
- **Given** the user has saved display name "Alice"
- **When** the page is reloaded
- **Then** the profile dialog shows "Alice", the header shows "Alice", and cards show "Alice"

### AC5: Consecutive renames work correctly
- **Given** the user has already renamed from "Alice Smith" → "Alice"
- **When** the user opens the profile again and renames to "A"
- **Then** the dialog, header, and all owned cards update to "A"

## Scope

### In Scope
- Fix the profile dialog to read the current display name from the Owners signal (not AuthContext `user.name`)
- After a successful save, update the AuthContext `user` state and localStorage cache with the new name
- Ensure the header user button reactively shows the current display name
- Ensure the cascade rename uses the correct "old" name from the Owners sheet

### Out of Scope
- Changing the Google account name itself (that's managed by Google)
- Multi-user real-time sync (if another user changes their name, the current user sees it on next board refresh — existing behavior is fine)
- Avatar/picture changes

## Technical Notes
- **Files likely affected:**
  - `frontend/src/components/board/kanban-board.tsx` — look up display name from `owners` signal instead of `user.name`
  - `frontend/src/components/profile/profile-dialog.tsx` — no changes expected (receives correct `currentName` prop)
  - `frontend/src/state/actions.ts` — `updateDisplayName()` needs to accept a `setUser` callback or similar to update AuthContext + localStorage
  - `frontend/src/auth/auth-provider.tsx` — may need to expose a `setUser` or `updateUserName` function via context
- **Complexity:** medium (4 files, state plumbing across context boundary)
- **Rules sync required:** no (display name logic is frontend-only)
- **Dependencies:** none — builds on existing #51 infrastructure

## Summary
Create a Claude Code skill that analyzes the project backlog to identify duplicates, merge related issues, and prune stale or obsolete items.

## Context
As the Hive project grows, the backlog accumulates issues that may overlap, duplicate each other, or become irrelevant. A dedicated agent skill (e.g., `/prune`) would automate backlog hygiene — saving time and keeping the board focused.

## Initial Scope
- New skill in `.claude/skills/prune/` that reads all open issues from the project board
- Detect duplicate or near-duplicate issues (similar titles, overlapping scope)
- Identify issues that could be combined into a single item
- Flag stale issues (no activity, outdated context)
- Present findings to the user for approval before taking action (close, merge, relabel)
- Actions: close duplicates with a linking comment, combine related issues, suggest removing stale items

## Open Questions
- Should the agent auto-close duplicates or only recommend and wait for approval?
- What similarity threshold to use for duplicate detection (title matching, body matching, or both)?
- Should it also re-prioritize or just prune?
- How should "combining" work — close one and update the other, or create a new combined issue?
